title: Discovery: Embeddings & Rerank - HighTorque
summary: Intro discovery to understand HighTorque's embedding + rerank needs: throughput, latency SLO, vector DB integration, hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC) and security requirements. Customers want a pilot to validate 1k qps embed pipeline and sub-100ms tail for rerank path. Action items: send pricing/TCO template, security docs, and schedule a 2-hour benchmarking session with sample dataset.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) tradeoffs
action_items: Maya: Share Redwood pricing template + simple TCO spreadsheet (due: 2026-04-23)
Liam: Send architecture note on VPC peering and Private deploy network flow (due: 2026-04-24)
Sofia: Provide sample traffic profile and 10k sample documents for benchmark (due: 2026-04-27)
next_steps: Schedule 2hr benchmarking session w/ sample dataset week of Apr 27
Send security pack (SOC2, ISO attestation, KMS integration guide)
Provide trial keys for Redwood Hosted + Dedicated pricing scenarios
Follow-up: 30-min deep-dive on vector DB connectors (Pinecone/FAISS/Redis)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-20 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (HighTorque Head of Search), Ethan Morales (HighTorque Platform), Sofia Delgado (Data Scientist)

Summary note: rough transcript, ASR has some small errors (e.g., product names, acronyms).

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood Inference, this is Liam our solutions engineer. quick round robin?
[00:08] Priya Rao: Hi all, Priya here - i run search at HighTorque. we have Ethan and Sofia on from infra and data.
[00:12] Ethan Morales: yep, Ethan, infra.
[00:15] Sofia Delgado: Sofia - data science.
[00:18] Maya Chen: awesome. main goal today is to understand your embedding + rerank workload and help land on hosted vs dedicated vs private. so maybe start with current stack and where pain points are.
[00:30] Priya Rao: sure. current stack is a hybrid: we compute embeddings offline with a mix of in-house models (mostly 1k dim) and sometimes use a managed service for ad-hoc features. vector store is currently FAISS on EKS nodes but it's creaking a bit - shards blow up during peak.
[00:45] Priya Rao: our real-time path is: query -> embed user query -> ANN search top 100 -> rerank with a small cross-encoder model for top 10. need tail latency under 150ms for the rerank step ideally <100ms if possible.
[00:58] Maya Chen: ok, good. when you say shards blow up - is that ingestion or query fanout?
[01:03] Priya Rao: mostly query fanout. spikes from campaigns or big search flows cause 100s of concurrent requests, our CPU based nodes can't keep up. storage I/O also becomes a bottleneck.
[01:15] Liam O'Connor: are you doing prefix caching or any KV cache for frequently asked queries?
[01:20] Sofia Delgado: we have a small Redis cache for hot queries but it's not very effective for long tails. the KV cache isn't hooked up to our ANN results; it's just query level.
[01:28] Liam O'Connor: got it. two things we typically see: embedding instrum - dimension choice matters a lot for throughput; and rerank costs scale with cross-encoder token length. what dimensionalities are you evaluating?
[01:40] Sofia Delgado: baseline is 1,024 dims for our production embedding, we're experimenting with 768 to save space and throughput. also looking at compact embeddings 256 via distillation for some flows.
[01:51] Maya Chen: good, and what's your QPS target for embeddings and rerank during peak?
[01:55] Priya Rao: embedding QPS around 1k sustained during business hours, spikes to ~3-4k for short bursts. rerank calls roughly ~600-800 qps (because we only rerank top candidates) but they're latency sensitive.
[02:07] Ethan Morales: and retention - we keep vectors for ~90 days hot, then archive. storage cost is non-trivial.
[02:12] Liam O'Connor: makes sense. so hosting choices: Redwood Hosted would give you fast time-to-value and we can manage autoscale for embedding and rerank, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput (good for sustained qps), Private gives you VPC/on-prem if compliance or network isolation required. any hard constraints for data residency or KMS?
[02:29] Priya Rao: we need company-owned keys via KMS for embeddings at rest and SSO integration. SOC2 is required for vendor. cloud region must be us-east or eu-west.
[02:38] Maya Chen: that's standard, we support customer-managed KMS and SAML SSO; SOC2 and ISO docs available. we'll include those in the security pack.
[02:45] Sofia Delgado: question on rerank: can Redwood host the cross-encoder on GPU for us and do batching to keep latency?
[02:51] Liam O'Connor: yes, we have GPU-optimized serving runtime that supports continuous batching and kernel selection; for cross-encoders we usually run them on A10/A100 like GPUs in Dedicated or on-hosted GPU fleet depending on SLA. batching does help but careful with tail latency.
[03:05] Priya Rao: what's a realistic tail latency for a cross-encoder on a dedicated GPU if we need top-10 rerank with ~512 token context?
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: rough numbers - single-request p99 for a 512 token cross-encoder on a gen GPU could be 80-200ms depending on quantization and batch size. with tuned batching and small batch sizes we can often get p95 <100ms, p99 can be closer to 150-200ms. we can run benchmarks on your exact model to get numbers.
[03:29] Priya Rao: ok that's useful. another concern: vector DB integration - we want to keep FAISS but also evaluate Pinecone for fallback. how does Redwood integrate with external vector stores?
[03:41] Maya Chen: Redwood supports connectors to common vector stores (Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, FAISS). we can route queries to your FAISS cluster or to our managed index; we also support hybrid search where ANN scores are combined with model-based rerank. fallback policies let you route to hosted variant when private capacity is constrained.
[04:00] Ethan Morales: about sharding - if we keep FAISS on our side, can Redwood's routing layer do fanout reduction or early stopping to avoid querying all shards?
[04:09] Liam O'Connor: yeah, we have smart routing and prefiltering - you can set shard-level routing policies and early termination thresholds. also prefix/KV caching can short-circuit for repeated queries.
[04:19] Speaker 2: [inaudible] latency spikes due to network hops sometimes.
[04:23] Maya Chen: network hops - that's where VPC peering and Private deployment help. with Private you can run the inference nodes in your VPC or on-prem with our control plane, reducing cross-network latency.
[04:34] Priya Rao: any cost ballpark for Dedicated capacity for our steady-state 1k embed qps and 800 rerank?
[04:40] Maya Chen: we need a quick sizing: embeddings can often be batched efficiently on multi-GPU nodes; for 1k qps embedding we might provision N GPUs depending on model dim and batch profiles. rerank is noisier - if you want reserved capacity to meet p95/p99 SLOs, that requires dedicated GPU pools. we'll send a TCO spreadsheet with example configurations (hosted vs dedicated) showing per-token math and reserved capacity pricing.
[05:00] Sofia Delgado: can you do quantized embeddings? we tried 8-bit quant and saw quality drop.
[05:06] Liam O'Connor: we support quantization profiles; some models compress well to 8-bit or 4-bit for storage/throughput but it depends on your evals. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload and we can run quality regression checks against your ground truth.
[05:18] Priya Rao: important for us to measure rerank quality change if we change embedding dims or quantization, that's part of the pilot success metric.
[05:25] Maya Chen: agreed. typical pilot success criteria we recommend: (1) embedding latency/throughput meets target QPS, (2) rerank tail latency within SLO, (3) retrieval+rerank relevance within X% of baseline on your eval set, (4) security and network requirements validated.
[05:40] Ethan Morales: what about burst handling? we have unpredictable spikes to 4k embed qps for a couple of minutes.
[05:46] Liam O'Connor: Dedicated supports burst policies and autoscale; Hosted will autoscale but there are cold-start windows. private on-prem is hardest for bursts unless you provision headroom. another pattern we recommend is hybrid routing: serve steady-state from Dedicated/Private and route bursts to Hosted fallback.
[06:02] Priya Rao: ok that hybrid idea might be ideal. how about A/B rollouts for model changes? we want canary reranks to compare new embedding dims.
[06:10] Maya Chen: Redwood Console supports rollouts, canary traffic splits, and metric comparisons. you can tie quality regression alerts to prompt sets and failover automatically.
[06:19] Sofia Delgado: network & compliance: we need audit logs for inference requests and token-level cost breakdown.
[06:25] Maya Chen: we've got token-level cost and tracing; audit logs are included and integrate with your SIEM. we'll include example log formats in the security pack.
[06:35] Priya Rao: any gotchas with KV cache for rerank? we worry about stale cached embeddings after model updates.
[06:42] Liam O'Connor: good callout - cache invalidation is important. Redwood supports TTLs and model-versioned cache keys so you can automatically evict on model rollouts.
[06:52] Priya Rao: nice. one more thing - does Redwood support per-tenant RBAC and row-level data scoping? we have multi-tenant product lines.
[07:00] Maya Chen: yes, we support RBAC, namespaces, and per-tenant isolation. Dedicated and Private give stronger guarantees for isolation.
[07:07] Speaker 3: [background]
[07:10] Sofia Delgado: for the pilot dataset - we'll send a 10k doc subset and a query workload sample. we want to see embedding storage footprint and rerank latency.
[07:18] Maya Chen: perfect. timeline-wise, if you share the dataset and traffic profile by next Monday we can schedule benchmarks the week after.
[07:25] Priya Rao: sounds good. what's the pilot duration you usually recommend?
[07:29] Liam O'Connor: 2-4 weeks for a proper pilot: initial benchmark + a short production-like run to validate autoscale and tail latency.
[07:36] Priya Rao: anything else we should be aware of on integration? we use Terraform heavily.
[07:41] Maya Chen: we have Terraform modules for Dedicated and VPC peering, and a quickstart repo. we'll share links.
[07:48] Ethan Morales: regarding vector DB connectors, will Redwood push embeddings to our FAISS clusters or do we need a sidecar?
[07:55] Liam O'Connor: both patterns supported: we can push via connector or you can run a small sidecar that receives embeddings and injects into FAISS. connectors handle schema mapping and shard routing.
[08:05] Priya Rao: ok. i'm a bit worried about vendor lock if we move heavy indexing into Redwood-managed store.
[08:11] Maya Chen: fair - that's why we emphasize abstraction: you can pin APIs and keep data ownership; fallback policies let you move between managed index and your self-hosted FAISS.
[08:21] Sofia Delgado: any initial recommendations for embedding dim for our use case (news-article retrieval + personalization)?
[08:27] Liam O'Connor: for news + personalization, 768-1024 is common; 256 compact can work for low-latency approximate rerank but expect some quality drop. recommend running a small sweep during pilot.
[08:38] Priya Rao: ok. last logistical Q: who should receive the security pack and pricing?
[08:43] Ethan Morales: send to me and Priya, cc security@hightorque.com.
[08:48] Maya Chen: will do. i'll send pricing + TCO and include Dedicated and Hosted scenarios. liam will send the VPC/how private deploy flow.
[08:56] Priya Rao: thanks. recap next steps?
[09:00] Maya Chen: recap: (1) HighTorque sends sample dataset + traffic profile (Sofia), (2) Redwood shares pricing/TCO and security docs (Maya), (3) SE note on VPC and connectors (Liam), (4) schedule 2hr benchmark (we'll propose slots).
[09:12] Priya Rao: perfect. thanks everyone.
[09:15] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcript: occasional ASR errors were present; abbreviations and product names may be slightly off in places.
